source_snapshots.notes: Descriptive national labour-market statistics with published definitions, metadata, and downloadable QLFS series. Not a causal crime estimate, local Johannesburg service-area baseline, or predictor of individual behavior.

Supports multidimensional measurement of decent work, including earnings, work safety, stability/security, and social protection. Does not set the viability fixture's numeric gates, create local legal requirements, or establish an effect on crime.

source_snapshots.observed_status: Governance, Public Safety and Justice Survey 2024/25 published on 2025-08-26; descriptive national victimization and reporting evidence
source_snapshots.notes: Victimization-survey reports and SAPS administrative reports are different observation processes. Offense-specific national reporting proportions help identify an observability problem but are not a local pilot rate or causal model coefficient.

source_snapshots.observed_status: Latest Victims of Crime Release in the GPSJS series; published 2026-09-01; reference period 2025/26
source_snapshots.notes: For housebreaking, estimated incidents rose from 1.493 million (2024/25) to 1.549 million (2025/26), while households experiencing it fell from 1.123 million to 1.078 million, and the share reporting some/all incidents rose from 43.4% to 48.2%. The technical notes report an 85.57% national response rate, a 76.97% Gauteng response rate (the lowest), and four geographic areas below the cited 80% minimum-acceptable response rate. Keep indicator denominators separate and use the estimate-specific precision/quality tables before significance claims; all reported trends remain descriptive national survey evidence, not causal effects or local pilot values.

cases.title: SANS reference found without context-specific incorporation evidence

forbidden_claims: this SANS is legally mandatory here
the repair is compliant

cases.rationale: Publication and national-standard status do not themselves establish legal incorporation or application to a particular project.

cases.title: ISO 37120 working draft must not be represented as a published edition

forbidden_claims: ISO 37120 Edition 3 is a published International Standard
conformance to Edition 3 can be certified

cases.rationale: ISO's catalogue lists ISO/WD 37120 as under development and intended to replace ISO 37120:2018; working drafts must remain distinct from published editions.

cases.title: Published ISO 37101 edition and draft replacement must coexist without silent supersession

forbidden_claims: the draft has already replaced the published edition
the older edition is withdrawn solely because a replacement is being drafted

cases.rationale: ISO's catalogue lists the 2016 edition and its 2024 amendment separately from the working draft intended to replace it. The record must preserve both instruments and their distinct lifecycle states.

cases.title: WCAG 2.2 publication does not prove local legal applicability

forbidden_claims: WCAG 2.2 automatically applies as binding law in South Africa
a checklist alone proves conformance

cases.rationale: W3C publication establishes the guideline/version and success-criteria framework; applicability as a legal duty requires a separate locally grounded analysis.

cases.title: Model law published internationally but local enactment not evidenced

forbidden_claims: publication of the model law proves domestic enactment

cases.rationale: A model law is not domestic legislation merely because an international body publishes it.

cases.title: Stale official snapshot cannot support a current applicability conclusion

forbidden_claims: this is the current deadline

cases.rationale: Old capture time is not a substitute for currentness verification, amendment history, and effective-date evidence.

cases.title: Directory listing does not prove provider competence or action authority

forbidden_claims: registry membership authorizes the action
registry membership proves competence

cases.rationale: Discovery and registry membership are evidence about the register's contents, not a blanket authorization grant.

cases.title: IETF RFC 9943 is a versioned technical reference, not a universal authority

forbidden_claims: a valid transparency receipt proves the signed statement is true
RFC conformance grants legal authority

cases.rationale: RFC 9943 describes a transparency architecture; transparency can make signed statements auditable but does not prevent dishonest or compromised issuers.

cases.title: NIST SP 800-82 Revision 4 initial public draft must not be called final or robot-certified

context.use_case: review OT cybersecurity controls for a proposed autonomous inspection robot at an essential-service facility

forbidden_claims: NIST SP 800-82 Revision 4 is a final publication
the draft automatically creates a binding South African legal obligation
catalogue or framework mapping proves the robot is secure or safe to operate
the reference satisfies a deployment-specific safety case

cases.rationale: The source is a point-in-time initial public draft. OT guidance can inform a risk review, but publication state, local legal applicability, technical conformance, and a deployment-specific robot safety case are distinct.

cases.title: UNODC crime-prevention guidance does not establish local legality or a robotics causal effect

context.use_case: choose a municipal intervention combining housing support, legitimate work pathways, and property-protection robots

forbidden_claims: the educational guidance is itself binding law for this municipality
a general crime-prevention typology proves that security robots reduce crime
the source authorizes person-level risk scoring or automated enforcement

cases.rationale: The source describes multiple prevention approaches. Local legal authority, intervention suitability, and causal efficacy require separate evidence and review.

cases.title: NIJ employment–crime findings must not be generalized into a universal robot-economy effect

context.use_case: estimate crime outcomes for an automation and employment program in a South African municipality

forbidden_claims: the historical U.S. study proves the local program will reduce crime
employment count alone establishes a causal effect
an urban-context finding necessarily generalizes to rural settings
the study qualifies autonomous robotics or Mycelix economic policy

cases.rationale: This research source can motivate a hypothesis, but the reported association is context-dependent. Local evaluation needs a defined intervention, outcomes, baseline, and credible counterfactual.

cases.title: Published industrial robot-cell standard must not be overgeneralized to a public-facing service or security robot

context.use_case: assess safety evidence for a public-facing municipal property-protection service robot

forbidden_claims: ISO 10218-2:2025 fully covers a public-access service robot
conformance to an industrial robot-cell standard proves this public-facing deployment is safe
the published standard establishes local legal permission for autonomous security intervention
industrial robot requirements apply universally to all service robots

cases.rationale: The official ISO catalogue describes ISO 10218-2:2025 as covering industrial robot applications and robot cells and lists public-access service robots and law-enforcement applications among exclusions. The publication status and industrial scope must be preserved; a different robot category requires separate hazard, standards-applicability, legal, and operational review.

cases.title: Stats SA national unemployment statistics must not be used as a local crime coefficient or individual propensity signal

context.use_case: decide whether the South African national unemployment statistic should calibrate a crime-prevention model or stand in for a Johannesburg service-area baseline

forbidden_claims: the national unemployment statistic is a causal crime coefficient
the QLFS national estimate is a Johannesburg service-area baseline without local evidence
national unemployment statistics predict an individual's criminal propensity
the QLFS statistic validates the simulator's synthetic crime parameters

cases.rationale: The QLFS is authoritative descriptive labour-market evidence for its target population and period. A model-specific causal estimate, local service-area baseline, and any individual inference are separate claims requiring different evidence and must not be fabricated from the national rate.

cases.title: The ILO decent-work measurement framework does not establish universal numeric viability thresholds or crime effects

input_projection.version: Decent Work Indicators — Concepts and Definitions; published 2013-12-18

context.use_case: choose measures and thresholds for an aggregate lawful-alternative viability contract in South Africa

forbidden_claims: the ILO framework establishes the prototype's universal 0.80 fair-pay adequacy threshold
the measurement framework is itself binding law for this service
decent-work indicators prove a causal reduction in crime
aggregate decent-work indicators authorize individual criminal-risk scoring

cases.rationale: The ILO source helps structure a multidimensional measurement plan. Local legal duties, community-approved adequacy benchmarks, data operationalization, and causal claims require separate evidence and review.

cases.title: Stats SA victimization and police-reporting measures must not be conflated with underlying harm

input_projection.version: Governance, Public Safety and Justice Survey 2024/25; published 2025-08-26

context.use_case: evaluate whether a decline in police-recorded incidents establishes a decline in victimization or a causal effect for an economic or robotics intervention

forbidden_claims: police-recorded incident counts measure all victimization
lower police-report counts alone prove fewer harmful incidents or a causal intervention effect
national offense-specific reporting proportions are a local service-area reporting rate without validation
the survey supplies a universal crime-effect coefficient or an individual risk signal

cases.rationale: Stats SA's 2024/25 publication reports offense-specific reporting patterns: 43.4% of households that experienced housebreaking reported some or all incidents, while 31% of people experiencing personal theft reported some or all incidents. These differing proportions show why police counts and victimization are not interchangeable. The survey is national context; local measurement, reporting dynamics, denominator compatibility, and a credible counterfactual remain necessary for evaluation.

cases.title: Latest GPSJS estimates require separating incident counts, affected households, and police reporting

input_projection.version: GPSJS 2025/26 Victims of Crime Release; published 2026-09-01

context.use_case: interpret year-over-year changes in household victimization and police reports without mixing counts, populations, and reporting processes

forbidden_claims: the rise in reported-housebreaking proportion from 43.4% to 48.2% proves housebreaking incidents fell
fewer households experiencing housebreaking necessarily means fewer incidents when estimated incidents rose from 1.493 million to 1.549 million
national 2025/26 reporting proportions are Johannesburg intervention outcomes or local reporting rates without local validation
the descriptive survey trend is a causal crime-effect coefficient or an individual risk signal

cases.rationale: Stats SA's latest 2025/26 release reports an estimated 1.549 million housebreaking incidents versus 1.493 million in 2024/25; households experiencing housebreaking fell from 1.123 million to 1.078 million; and households reporting some or all housebreaking incidents rose from 43.4% to 48.2%. These are distinct indicators with different denominators. Survey estimates need their definitions, sample design and precision limits preserved, and they do not establish an intervention effect or a Johannesburg baseline.

cases.title: Survey response-rate and precision limits must gate year-over-year significance claims

input_projection.version: GPSJS 2025/26 Victims of Crime Release technical notes; published 2026-09-01

context.use_case: interpret national and provincial year-over-year victimization estimates without overstating precision, significance, or local relevance

forbidden_claims: the rise from 43.4% to 48.2% is statistically significant because rounded point estimates differ
Gauteng estimates are invalid solely because the province response rate was 76.97%
the 85.57% national response rate guarantees precision for every province or subgroup
the cited 80% minimum-acceptable response rate is a statistical-significance threshold or substitutes for estimate-specific confidence intervals
year-over-year survey point estimates prove that a local robotics or economic intervention caused a crime outcome
the 3% coefficient of variation for Table 41 household housebreaking experience is the precision estimate for the distinct 43.4% to 48.2% police-reporting proportion
the Table 41 prevalence estimates of 43.1% in 2024/25 and 46.0% in 2025/26, each with a 3% coefficient of variation, by themselves establish statistical significance
a 4.8 percentage-point difference between rounded police-reporting proportions is statistically significant without precision estimates for those reporting proportions

cases.rationale: Stats SA's 2025/26 GPSJS technical notes report an 85.57% national household response rate, 76.97% for Gauteng, 73.72% for the City of Johannesburg, and 67.54% for the City of Tshwane; four geographic areas fell below the cited 80% minimum-acceptable level in Stats SA 019:2017 V2.00. These response rates are quality diagnostics, not significance tests and not proof that every estimate from a lower-response area is invalid. Before stating that a difference is statistically meaningful, preserve the indicator's definition and denominator, survey design and weighting, time comparability, geographic scope, and the published estimate-specific standard error, confidence interval, coefficient of variation, or other precision information where available. A city-level response rate is not itself an estimate-precision statistic. National descriptive survey changes do not establish a local baseline or causal intervention effect. Table 41's published precision figures are explicitly tracked as a different indicator: household housebreaking experience in the past 12 months was 43.1% (CV 3%) in 2024/25 and 46.0% (CV 3%) in 2025/26. Those CVs are not the precision estimate for the distinct share reporting housebreaking incidents to police (43.4% to 48.2%), and the CVs alone are not a test of the difference.
